ov: The smallest birds, about 375 species native to the Americas. Their wings allow helicopter-like flight in any direction, and the hum of their wingbeats gives them their name.

why.d: Specialised for nectar from flowers, but every species also eats small insects.

len: 5 cm (bee hummingbird) to 13 cm for most
rg: The Americas, from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego.
df: Nectar from flowers, plus small insects.
fx: To save energy at night or when food is scarce, it can enter torpor, slowing its metabolism to a fifteenth of normal.
notes: Group entry. REGION: animals.js r is North and South America; Alaska to Tierra del Fuego includes Central America. Consider adding it. ANSWER CHECK (fact): the animals.js fact "The only bird that can fly backwards" isn’t supported. Wikipedia says hummingbirds can fly in any direction, but not that they’re the only ones. Suggested wording: "Can fly in any direction, even backwards, beating its wings up to 99 times a second." RESOLVED: animals.js fact rewritten to "Can fly in any direction, even backwards, beating its wings up to 99 times a second." Region added.
